domains.name: Address Code
domains.comment: Value pattern /^A-[0-9]{4,}$/ - an opaque surrogate. Recorded as a note rather than a value constraint: CaseTalk value constraints enumerate values, ranges and state transitions, they do not hold regular expressions.

domains.name: British Postcode
domains.comment: Mandatory for a GB thoroughfare address together with post town. Separate label type from the Dutch postcode because the formats and the identification semantics differ.

domains.name: CEP
domains.comment: Value pattern /^[0-9]{5}-[0-9]{3}$/. Bairro is handled through Address Admin Unit with an Admin Level Kind of BAIRRO rather than its own role.

domains.name: Dutch Postcode
domains.comment: Value pattern /^[1-9][0-9]{3}[A-Z]{2}$/. DR1/DR2: thoroughfare and administrative unit/place are CONSEQUENCES of postcode plus premise number, not independent facts - storing them as independent roles guarantees a reconciliation backlog that never empties. Composite identification (UC2) for a Dutch thoroughfare address is {postcode, premise number, premise number addition}: an identification spanning three fact types, which is not placeable as one intra-fact UC.

domains.name: Paradigm Code
domains.valueconstraint: BLOCK, CODE, LANDMARK, POSTBOX, PROVISIONAL, THOROUGHFARE

domains.name: Spanish Postal Code
domains.comment: Value pattern /^[0-5][0-9]{4}$/. Composite identification (UC3) is {thoroughfare type, thoroughfare, premise number, stair, floor, door, municipality} - spanning several fact types, so not placeable as one intra-fact UC.

tables.name: Address
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A designation by which a location can be identified for delivery, legal or administrative purposes. Identified by an opaque surrogate (Address Code) - not a value, not a composite key, not a per-country type. Every real identification scheme in the world (postcode+number, Eircode, UPRN, chome/banchi/go) is a FACT ABOUT an address, not the address itself; making any of them the identifier imports one jurisdiction assumptions into the identity of the concept. What is universally true of an address is only this: it has an identity, it is in a country, it follows some addressing paradigm, and it can be rendered as an ordered sequence of lines.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " follows paradigm <Address Paradigm_Paradigm Code>Paradigm <Address Code>Address "
  " designates <Address Location Designation_Location Code>Location <Address Code>Address "
  " is located in <Address Country_Country Code>Country <Address Code>Address "
  " superseded <Address Code>Address <PredecessorAddress_Address Code>Address "
  " was produced by  with confidence <Structuring_Confidence><Structuring_Derivation Source Code>Derivation Source <Address Code>"
* " has verification status <Address Verification Status><Address Code>"
  " has postal place name <Address Postal Place Name><Address Code>Address "
[Rules]
"Population supports Valid Time"
"<Address> is identified by <Address Code>"
"<Address Code> in <Address> is a subset of <Address Code> in <Address>"
"<Address Code> in <Address> is a subset of <Address Code> in <Rendering Line Position>"

columns.name: Address Paradigm_Paradigm Code
columns.comment: Which paradigm an address follows changes over time - the lot-to-street transition forced by the Australian population. The transition is NOT the destruction and recreation of the address, which would lose the continuity every downstream system needs; it is a new period of validity on the same address. Carried by the Valid Time flag on this fact type rather than by a date role, because the date only records when the assignment became true.

columns.name: PredecessorAddress_Address Code
columns.comment: Street renames, municipal mergers, lot-to-street transitions and country dissolutions are all the same shape, and together with the Valid Time flag on Address this carries the whole temporal burden. Acyclicity is required over the transitive closure. This is the piece to build first, because it is the only one that cannot be retrofitted.

columns.name: Address Postal Place Name
columns.comment: Deliberately NOT the administrative unit. In the United States the USPS preferred city name is routinely not the incorporated municipality: an address may be postally Beverly Hills and municipally Los Angeles. Collapsing the two breaks tax jurisdiction and sales territory assignment in the same stroke, and the breakage stays invisible until an auditor finds it.

columns.name: Address Verification Status
columns.comment:
[Derivation]
Latest outcome per Address from Address Registry Check, taking the instance with the maximal check date; UNVERIFIED where no check instance exists. Not stored: a boolean verified flag erodes in meaning, whereas an outcome plus its date can always be re-derived.
[Comment]
Derived, not stored. UNVERIFIED where no check instance exists. A large fraction of addresses in an international population can never be validated against any registry at all, so the absence of a check is itself information and must not be conflated with a failed check.

A landmark is therefore not a variant type of address; it is an optional fact that can attach to several.

tables.name: Address Without Premise Number
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A positive assertion that this premise has been assigned NO number - Brazilian s/n, sem numero. Entirely different from "we do not know the number". A nullable column expresses neither and cannot tell them apart, and the distinction becomes unresolvable the moment a delivery exception is raised. Exclusive with Address Premise Number.

[Rules]

"<Address Without Premise Number> is a subset of <Address Code> in <Thoroughfare Address>"

tables.name: CR Landmark Address
tables.comment: Identity here is relative and depends on another object lifecycle. There is no postal code role and no premise number role; the nearest thing to a stable identifier is the landmark, and the landmark can be cut down. At least one of Address Landmark Qualification or Address Landmark Distance is required - but those roles are played by Address (the supertype, deliberately, per the India argument), so the requirement cannot be scoped to this subtype as a set constraint and is recorded here.

columns.name: Address Door
columns.comment: The vertical component participates in identity. Two Spanish addresses differing only in door are as distinct as two differing in house number, so floor and door cannot be relegated to an unstructured "unit" line without losing uniqueness - and that is exactly the reflex of models built in countries with mostly-detached housing.

tables.name: GB Thoroughfare Address
tables.comment: Number or building name, at least one: "Rose Cottage, Nether Poppleton, York" is a complete, deliverable, unambiguous address containing no number whatsoever. That disjunction spans two object types - Address Premise Number is played by Thoroughfare Address while Address Building Name is played by this subtype - so it cannot be expressed as one set constraint and is recorded here. Post town and postcode are both mandatory.

columns.name: Address Eircode_Eircode Value
columns.comment: The identifier portion is deliberately non-geographic and unordered: neighbouring dwellings share nothing beyond the routing key. Nothing below the routing key is derivable from the code, and the code is derivable from nothing else. Before Eircode the descriptive facts genuinely did not identify - dozens of dwellings in one townland shared identical address text. That historical population is worth keeping as a live example of a designation that fails to designate.

columns.name: Address Routing Key
columns.comment:
[Derivation]
First three characters of the Eircode. The routing key is the only part of an Eircode that carries geography.

columns.name: Address Unique Identifier
columns.comment:
[Derivation]
Last four characters of the Eircode. Deliberately non-geographic and unordered - neighbouring dwellings share nothing beyond the routing key.

tables.name: JP Block Address
tables.comment: Address Thoroughfare is not optional here, it is INAPPLICABLE. Numbering proceeds by block within a named area, and in older districts numbering within a block follows registration order rather than geography, so adjacency in the data implies nothing about adjacency in the world; most Japanese streets have no name at all. This single population is the clearest justification for subtyping over one wide optional type - a wide type would carry a street role that can never be truthfully filled for tens of millions of addresses. Large buildings hold their own postal code, sometimes floor-specific, which is why the postal code attaches to the address rather than deriving from the admin unit.

Three roles fix an arbitrary cardinality into the schema, leave most of the population with empty roles, and force a migration the first time a Japanese building name and floor push an address to six lines. The sequence must be gapless and every rendering has a line 1.

tables.name: Usage
tables.comment:
[Definition]
The use a party makes of an address - billing, shipping, registered office, place of birth, tax residence. The role of use belongs to the connecting fact type, never to the address. Put usage inside Address and no address instance is ever reusable, deduplication becomes impossible, and the constraint that a registered office may not be a post box cannot be expressed at all.

  " uses <Address Code> as <Usage Kind Code>Usage Kind <Party Code>Party "
[Rules]
"Population supports Valid Time"
"<Usage> is identified by <Address Code>, <Party Code> and <Usage Kind Code>"
"<Address Code> in <Usage> is a subset of <Address Code> in <Address>"

tables.name: Usage Assertion
tables.comment: The communication-oriented heart of the model. An address supplied by a customer is not a fact about the world; it is a statement made by a party at a moment, and it may be wrong. Modelled as a plain attribute of Party, the statement and its truth are fused; modelled as a fact with an asserter and a date they separate - and verification against a registry becomes another fact with its own date and outcome rather than a boolean flag whose meaning erodes.

"<Usage Kind Code>, <Address Code>, <Party Code> in <Usage Assertion> is a subset of <Usage>"
